relevance_note: Retrospective series of four children with HA20 and germline TNFAIP3 variants: "Genetic testing identified TNFAIP3 mutations in all four patients".
method_note:
Read the whole paper by hand. Tables 1-3 have patients as columns under the header "|  | Patient 1 | Patient 2 | Patient 3 | Patient 4 |"; per-patient spans quote the row from its label through that patient's cell. A short Python script (own scratch dir) assembled the JSON from my readings and cut the table-row spans; I checked every scripted cell value against the tables (Table 1 "−" = "Negative"; Table 2 "−" = "Normal", "/" = not done). The Table 2 bold marking of abnormal values was lost in conversion, so lab values outside printed ranges that the text does not describe (ALB in Patients 2-4, LDH in Patients 2-4, NE in Patient 4, ESR 19 in Patient 3) were not turned into features.
Individuals: 4 patients plus the tested, wild-type parents of Patients 1, 3 and 4 (6 rows). The paper refers to these parents only collectively ("her parents", "wild-type parents", "both parents"), so their labels ("Patient k, parent 1/2") are constructed, and sex is not reported. No parent result is described for Patient 2, so no parent rows for Patient 2. is_proband for Patients 2-4 rests on the Methods sentence about "the proband’s phenotype"; Patient 1 is called "the proband" in Fig. 1C.
Contradictions and judgment calls:
(1) Patient 4 cDNA: c.1243_1247del in the abstract, Results text, Fig. 4C, ACMG sentence and Discussion, but c.1247_1251del in Table 3 (protein p.(Asn416Thrfs*11) and the 5-bp hg19 interval agree in both). Recorded c.1243_1247del; not resolved.
(2) Rheumatoid factor: text says "Autoantibody panels, rheumatoid factor, skin prick test and pathogen screening were negative", but Table 2 gives "RF-IgA elevated" for Patients 1, 2 and 4. Both rows emitted for those three; the autoantibodies checklist item is "not reported" for them. Patient 3 RF "Negative" in both, so autoantibodies excluded for Patient 3.
(3) Patient 3 variant novelty: "Patients 1, 3, and 4 carried novel frameshift or nonsense mutations" vs "This variants has been previously reported [5, 6]" and the abstract's "one previously reported mutation (c.133C > T)". The paper does not say Patient 3 was described before, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null; reference 6 (Liu P, Wang YS, et al., Zhonghua Er Ke Za Zhi 2020, a single child with infantile-onset IBD and a heterozygous TNFAIP3 mutation) shares an author name with this paper's last author, so a re-report is possible and should be checked at deduplication.
(4) Patient 2 inheritance: Table 3 says "de novo", but no parental result is described for the deletion (the parental-testing sentence and Figs. 1C/3B/4C cover only the other three variants). Under rule 8 inheritance is "not reported"; the table entry and the Methods sentence on WES of first-degree relatives are in parental_testing_statement.
(5) Patient 2 deletion is called heterozygous (2.18 Mb, 6q23.3, 13 genes incl. TNFAIP3, PEX7, IL20RA, IL22RA2), yet the Discussion groups it with "complete A20 deficiency" / "complete A20 loss". Recorded as one heterozygous large deletion; the other deleted genes are not separate variant rows.
(6) Anemia: "all four patients demonstrated anemia", but Patient 4 HGB is 110 g/L against a printed range of 110-150; recorded as observed from the group statement, with the value in detail.
(7) Abstract says "lymphadenopathy in one case", but Table 2 shows lymph node enlargement in Patient 1 (CT) and Patient 4 (ultrasound); both recorded. Abstract says arthritis in 50% of patients, Table 1 shows arthritis only in Patient 2.
(8) "Imaging revealed intestinal mucosal edema in all patients (4/4)", but Table 2's ultrasound cell for Patient 2 shows only the knee; Patient 2's mucosal edema is recorded as inferred from the group statement. Table 2's "Abdominal MRI" row for Patient 2 describes the knee.
(9) Patient 2 marrow signal: text says "suggestive of active hematopoiesis" / "compensatory erythroid hyperplasia", while Fig. 2C says "Bone tissue inflammation in femur and lower leg bones"; both recorded.
(10) "T/B lymphopenia in Patients 1 and 2" (Discussion) while Table 2 gives "CD8 + T cells increased" for Patient 1; both recorded.
(11) "intermittent fever and perianal aphthosis" (abstract, unnamed) are attributed to Patient 1 because Patient 1 is the only patient given IFX and azathioprine. "Lumbosacral MRI showed no abnormalities" names no patient and was not recorded.
Checklist calls: "Oral/Genital aphthosis −" taken as excluding oral/genital ulcers because the paper uses "aphthosis" for ulcers (e.g. "gastric aphthosis in Patient 2" = Table 2 "Gastric ulcer"). "Skin eruption −" (Patients 1, 3) and "Arthritis −" (Patients 1, 3, 4) leave the composite skin and arthritis/arthralgia items "not reported". "Hepatic injury −" excludes autoimmune hepatitis for Patients 1-3; Patient 4's transient liver injury is not called autoimmune, so "not reported". Anemia is attributed to gastrointestinal bleeding, so "cytopenia (autoimmune)" is "not reported" for all. Recurrent fever: Table 1 "Fever +" per patient plus the abstract's "All four patients ... recurrent fever".
